quote: The Williams Geismar Olefins Plant, which employs approximately 110 people, is located in Geismar, Louisiana, approximately 20 miles southeast of Baton Rouge.
value: ~110 people; ~20 miles SE of Baton Rouge

quote: The Lummus Company designed and built the olefins plant in 1967, and Allied Chemical first operated it.
value: 1967 built by Lummus; Allied Chemical first operator

quote: In 1985, Union Texas Petroleum purchased the plant from Allied Chemical and sold it to Atlantic Richfield Company (ARCO) in 1998. Williams then purchased the facility in 1999.
value: 1985 Union Texas; 1998 ARCO; 1999 Williams; at incident jointly owned Williams Olefins LLC and SABIC, Williams sole operator

quote: The plant originally produced 600 million pounds of ethylene annually.
Over the years, the production capacity increased to 1.35 billion pounds of ethylene and 80 million pounds of propylene per year.

At the time of the incident, approximately 800 contractors worked at the Williams Geismar facility on an expansion project, with an end goal of increasing the production of ethylene to 1.95 billion pounds per year.
The reboiler that failed, EA-425B ("Reboiler B") was one of two reboilers (Reboiler A and Reboiler B) that supplied heat to the propylene fractionator
value: EA-425B Reboiler B; paired with Reboiler A serving propylene fractionator

quote: Reboiler B had been offline for 16 months while Reboiler A was in operation, but was clean and available for use when Reboiler A eventually fouled
where tube-side hot quench water vaporizes shell-side hydrocarbon process fluid, which is approximately 95% propane with the balance composed mostly of propylene and C4s
(This report refers to the propane mixture as "propane.")

item: Quench water inlet temperature to reboilers
quote: Quench water enters the propylene fractionator reboilers at approximately 185 °F
which enters the reboiler at a temperature of approximately 130 °F
In 2001, Williams installed valves on the shell-side and tube-side reboiler piping to allow for continuous operation with only one reboiler operating at a time.
The original propylene fractionator design had both reboilers continuously operating.
value: original: both continuously operating; modified: one operating, one isolated standby

quote: The heat exchangers are 24 feet 8 inches long end-to-end.
Each exchanger shell (the portion of the heat exchanger that holds the tube bundle) is approximately 18.5 feet long and over 5 feet in diameter.
The tubes are each ¾-inch in diameter, and each heat exchanger contains 3,020 tubes.
if one were to lay each tube from one heat exchanger end-to-end in a straight line, the tubes would span over 10.5 miles.
Depicted in Figure 3 as a two-pass heat exchanger for purposes of simplicity, the reboilers were six-pass heat exchangers.
The valves (gate valves) isolating the reboilers from the pressure relief valve at the top of the propylene fractionator were not part of the original design, and were installed in 2001.
value: gate valves isolate reboilers from column-top relief; added 2001

quote: The quench water that directly contacts the heated furnace effluent gases is part of a closed-loop water circulation system.

item: Quench water settler and fouling mechanism
quote: The quench water settler removes most of the tar material (Figure 2); however, some oily material remains in the quench water.
value: settler removes most tar; residual oily material causes fouling

quote: Over time, some of this material adheres to and builds up on the inside of process equipment such as heat exchanger tubes, resulting in a decrease in both heat transfer efficiency and quench water flow rate.
value: fouling = buildup reducing heat transfer and flow

quote: the quench water flow through the operating propylene fractionator reboiler (Reboiler A) had dropped gradually over the past day (Figure 5).
value: gradual drop over past day in Reboiler A quench flow

item: Initiating valve opening time and evidence
quote: The CSB determined that at 8:33 am, the operations supervisor likely opened the quench water valves on the offline reboiler, Reboiler B, as indicated by the rapid increase in quench water flow rate shown in Figure 6.
value: 8:33 am likely opened B tube-side quench valves

quote: Approximately three minutes later, Reboiler B exploded (Figure 7).
The force of the explosion launched a portion of the propylene fractionator reboiler piping into a pipe rack approximately 30 feet overhead (Figure 8).
Quench water flow rate rises when Reboiler B tube-side quench water valves are opened. Reboiler B ruptures approximately three minutes later.
A Williams operator working near the propylene fractionator at the time of the explosion died at the scene. The operations supervisor succumbed to severe burn injuries the next day.
167 personnel reported injuries. / Of the 167 workers who reported injuries, three were Williams employees and 164 were contractors.
The fire lasted approximately 3.5 hours, and Williams reported releasing over 30,000 pounds of flammable hydrocarbons during the incident.
The plant remained down for 18 months and restarted in January 2015.
